slides.title: Network Cabling & Connectors
content: Network cabling is the physical medium used to transfer data between devices, while connectors link cables to devices for proper signal transmission
Twisted Pair cables use copper wires twisted together to reduce interference and are commonly used in Ethernet networks with RJ45 connectors
Fiber Optic cables transmit data as light signals, providing high speed and long-distance communication using connectors like LC and SC
Coaxial cables use a central conductor with shielding to reduce interference and are used in cable TV and broadband with BNC and F-type connectors

slides.title: Network Devices
content: Network devices are hardware components that enable communication, data transfer, and connectivity between devices in a network
They help in routing, switching, signal amplification, and maintaining efficient and reliable communication
Each device operates at different layers of the OSI model and performs specific networking functions
Examples include routers, switches, hubs, bridges, and repeaters

slides.title: Router, Switch, Hub
content: A router connects multiple networks and routes data packets using IP addresses while providing internet access and security features like NAT
A switch connects devices within the same network and forwards data using MAC addresses to ensure efficient communication
A hub is a basic device that broadcasts data to all connected devices without filtering, operating at the physical layer
Switches are more efficient than hubs as they reduce unnecessary network traffic

slides.title: Bridge & Repeater
content: A bridge connects multiple networks and divides large networks into smaller segments while filtering traffic using MAC addresses
A repeater amplifies and regenerates signals to extend the transmission distance in a network
Both devices operate at lower layers of the OSI model to improve network performance and reliability
They are commonly used to expand networks and maintain signal integrity over long distances

slides.title: Ethernet Frame Structure
content: An Ethernet frame is the basic unit of data transmission in Ethernet networks that encapsulates data for communication
It includes fields like Preamble and Start Frame Delimiter to synchronize and mark the beginning of the frame
Source and Destination MAC addresses identify sender and receiver devices within a network
Payload carries actual data while Frame Check Sequence (FCS) ensures error detection and data integrity

slides.title: Functions of Ethernet Frame
content: Ethernet frames perform data encapsulation by packaging data for transmission across the network
They ensure accurate delivery using MAC addressing and error detection through CRC in the FCS field
They help in managing network communication and flow control to prevent congestion
They support reliable communication across LANs and interconnected networks
